strategies.title: ordered attempt [batched-greedy-state-evolution] Target-residual greedy packing candidate
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: batched-greedy-state-evolution

Replacement scope: Replace the single LPT branch of `balanced_packing` with a three-way selector consisting of the current LPT branch, the current cyclic branch, and one target-residual greedy branch; do not change replication or hierarchy logic.

Compute budget: One extra batched greedy pass of exactly `num_groups` transitions, zero restarts, and zero post-packing iterations. Each transition performs one masked `argmin`, two gathers/scatters, and one load update across all layers; expected algorithm time increase is approximately one additional existing LPT pass.

Gain mechanism: LPT chooses the currently least-loaded non-full pack without considering whether assigning the next descending item will overshoot the unavoidable mean load. The added branch computes each layer’s target pack load `sum(weight) / num_packs` and, for each sorted group, chooses among non-full packs by lexicographically minimizing `(max(0, current_load + item - target), current_load)`. Thus it preferentially fills a pack that remains below target and uses ordinary least-load behavior only when every feasible placement overshoots. This supplies a different greedy decision surface from LPT while maintaining exact cardinality and batched execution.

Use float64 CPU accumulators exactly as in the current LPT implementation. For each position, form `projected = pack_load + sorted_weight[:, position]`, mask full packs to infinity in both keys, derive the primary excess key by `clamp_min(projected - target[:, None], 0)`, select the minimum excess and then minimum current load among ties, assign rank from `pack_count`, and update state. Compare all candidate layouts by the existing exact peak-then-squared-load objective before returning. The output remains a complete permutation with valid contiguous ranks in every pack.

Expected-gain check: accept this direction only if evaluation reports `combined_score > 0.146804633399`; the test is falsifiable because target-residual selection can choose a non-minimum-load destination that incumbent LPT cannot choose when doing so avoids a larger target overshoot.

strategies.title: [three-cycle-bottleneck-descent] Critical three-pack rotation refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: three-cycle-bottleneck-descent

Replacement scope: Replace the final candidate-selection portion of `balanced_packing`, after LPT and cyclic layouts have been built, with a bounded exact three-pack rotation refinement initialized from the better of those two layouts.

Compute budget: One deterministic start per layer; at most 2 refinement passes; in each pass inspect only the current heaviest pack, the two lightest distinct packs, and the 8 heaviest groups in each participating pack. Evaluate at most 8 × 8 × 8 × 2 rotations per pass and accept the lexicographically best strict improvement. Expected evaluation-time effect: small CPU overhead only when `groups_per_pack > 1`, bounded independently of the total number of groups after the initial sort.

Gain mechanism: LPT and cyclic packing can only choose a destination independently for each group during construction. A capacity-preserving three-cycle can reduce the maximum GPU or node load when no pairwise exchange is improving: move one large group out of the bottleneck pack, route a medium group through a second pack, and use a light compensating group from the third pack to preserve all exact per-pack cardinalities. This escape direction is unavailable to either existing construction.

Build the best existing LPT/cyclic layout exactly as today, reconstruct per-pack group lists from `pack_index` and `rank_in_pack`, and for each candidate ordered triple of packs evaluate both directed rotations of one selected group from each pack. Update the three affected loads analytically, accept only a strict improvement in `(maximum pack load, sum of squared pack loads)`, and update exactly those three `pack_index`/`rank_in_pack` entries. Retain the original candidate if no strict refinement exists. Cardinality remains valid because every rotation removes and inserts exactly one group in each involved pack; every group continues to have one pack and one rank, so downstream inverse permutations remain valid. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring `combined_score > 0.146804633399`; the incumbent cannot realize a strict capacity-preserving directed three-pack rotation after either of its one-pass constructions.

strategies.title: [load-aware-group-synthesis] Mesoscopic balanced group formation before node pac
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: load-aware-group-synthesis

Replacement scope: Replace the fixed contiguous `weight.unflatten(-1, (num_groups, group_size)).sum(-1)` group construction in the hierarchical branch of `rebalance_experts_hierarchical`; retain replica construction and physical GPU packing unchanged.

Compute budget: None beyond one per-layer expert sort and two scatter operations. Construct one additional hierarchy candidate and compare it with the existing fixed-group hierarchy and global-pool candidate using the existing `placement_proxy`. Expected evaluation-time effect: one extra sort of `num_logical_experts` values per layer, with no iterative optimizer.

Gain mechanism: The current hierarchy treats adjacent logical expert IDs as immutable groups, so a contiguous run of heavy experts becomes an indivisible high-load node-group before node packing begins. The replacement synthesizes equal-cardinality groups by sorted-rank interleaving: sort experts descending by load, place rank `r` in synthesized group `r % num_groups`, and assign in-group rank `r // num_groups`. Consequently each group gets one expert from each load quantile and all groups retain exactly `group_size` experts. Node packing is then operating on balanced mesoscopic units rather than accidental ID-contiguous heavy clusters.

Construct `synth_log2mlog` directly from the sorted expert indices, with group position `group_id * group_size + rank_in_group`; derive its inverse using the existing `inverse` helper. Run the existing replication and GPU packing pipeline with this synthesized mapping. Do not replace the existing construction unconditionally: form this as a third complete feasible candidate and use the current lexicographic placement proxy to choose among fixed hierarchy, synthesized hierarchy, and global pool. All output invariants are retained because `synth_log2mlog` is a permutation, groups have exact cardinality, and replication/rank bookkeeping is unchanged. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring `combined_score > 0.146804633399`; unlike the incumbent, this candidate can separate two adjacent heavy logical experts into different node groups before any node-level capacity decision.

strategies.title: [cardinality-constrained-differencing] Differencing-based GPU bundle constructio
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: cardinality-constrained-differencing

Replacement scope: Replace the GPU-level call to `balanced_packing(tokens_per_phy, num_gpus // num_nodes)` inside `rebalance_experts_hierarchical` with a portfolio containing the current packing result and a cardinality-constrained differencing result; preserve the lower-load candidate according to the same peak-then-squared-load objective.

Compute budget: One deterministic differencing start per layer and per node-local physical-expert pool; no restarts; at most `num_physical_experts // num_nodes - 1` heap/differencing merges plus a bounded cardinality repair involving at most 16 items around the two most imbalanced resulting packs. Expected evaluation-time effect: linearithmic in physical experts for this extra candidate and no dependence on replica count beyond the already present physical slots.

Gain mechanism: LPT makes irrevocable one-item placement decisions against current load totals, while cyclic packing ignores values after sorting. Cardinality-constrained differencing instead constructs opposite-sign bundles of large and small replica loads so that cancellation is represented explicitly before GPU labels are assigned. This gives a qualitatively different global arrangement: a high-load replica can be deliberately paired with the aggregate complement of several lower-load replicas rather than merely sent to the presently least-loaded GPU.

For each layer, start from singleton signed bundles carrying `(positive_count, negative_count, signed_load)` and repeatedly difference the two greatest-magnitude bundles, tracking exact item membership. During reconstruction, assign signs to GPU sides while enforcing exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` physical slots per GPU. For more than two GPUs, recursively split the current bundle set into two GPU subsets whose required slot counts sum correctly, using the same constrained differencing construction. If a split has an off-by-cardinality repair, exchange only members in the two affected partitions and select the repair minimizing the resulting peak and squared loads. Convert final GPU memberships to `pack_index` and stable in-pack ranks. Keep the current `balanced_packing` result whenever its exact objective is better. Every GPU receives exactly its required number of physical slots, and the output remains a permutation, so `inverse`, `pphy2phy`, and `log2phy` validity are preserved. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring `combined_score > 0.146804633399`; the incumbent has no representation of signed aggregate complements and therefore cannot produce a differencing partition unless it happens accidentally through its greedy decisions.
